answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a fixed token bond for 90 days before it can bid on jobs, whether compiling an atlas, pricing timber, or scheduling irrigation at an oasis. The same tokens cannot back two identities at once. An attacker creating 1,000 eligible agents must therefore lock 1,000 bonds, tying up capital and forgoing its use elsewhere for the full period; generating new keys alone buys no access.
